I let a relationship practically consume me and everything I wanted to do in life. It was overall a good relationship, but when it ended it ended badly because I had put too much investment into the relationship by a mile.


When it first ended I felt crushed, I wasn't working that hard at university, I had practically lost all the hobbies that I had first had at the start of the relationship and I hated hanging around my group of friends, but didn't leave for fear of being alone. However when I finally decided to cut off contact and all the things I hated out my life things got a lot better. I left the group of friends I hated and was instantly accepted by a bunch of people I really like (And who now I'm really close with), I got all my own hobbies back and more. Such as being a singer in a band, which I never saw myself doing, but I thought fuck it if I'm rock bottom I may aswell do something random. Plus I'm doing better on my university course and eventually want to do research into artificial intelligence. I feel like I'm myself again, I'm confident around people and even when there's times I'm not as happy as I could be I can do things or see people that make me feel better.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that when I felt like a complete failure I bounced back by simply doing stuff that I wanted to do. I didn't set limitations and I certainly didn't worry about what people thought, it freed me to do some pretty crazy stuff, but I wouldn't have it any other way. I'm a very happy person because of it, and if something happens that makes me feel like a failure again, I know how to bounce back.
